## 任务：撰写论文 Experiments 章节 (§4)

### 写作前必读
1. `Read /home/ubuntu/agent-ml-research/skills/global/latex-paper.skill.md` — LaTeX 写作规范
2. `Read /home/ubuntu/agent-ml-research/skills/global/red-section.skill.md` — 写作红线

### 论文背景
**标题**: "When Does Non-Uniform KV Cache Quantization Help? Cardinality Constraints and a Heterogeneity Diagnostic"
**Venue**: EMNLP 2026 Main (ARR), 8 pages
**Core claim**: 一个 cardinality constraint (max_2bit≤k) 修复 hardware-aligned {2,4,8,16} 上的 per-head KV cache quantization 失败。收益与 head sensitivity heterogeneity 正相关。

### 章节结构与 Word Budget
~1200 words total. 5 subsections:

### §4.1 Experimental Setup (~250 words)

**模型**:
- Qwen2.5-7B: GQA ratio 7:1, 28 layers × 4 KV heads = 112 KV heads
- Llama-3.1-8B: GQA ratio 4:1, 32 layers × 8 KV heads = 256 KV heads
- Mistral-7B-v0.3: GQA ratio 4:1, 32 layers × 8 KV heads = 256 KV heads, sliding window attention

**评估**:
- Dataset: WikiText-2 test split (298,938 tokens)
- Metric: perplexity (PPL, ↓ better), bf16 inference, stride=512
- 下游任务: ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag, PIQA, WinoGrande (0-shot)

**Profiling**:
- Per-head PPL-based distortion: quantize each head independently to each bit-width, measure PPL increase
- Hires calibration: 64 sequences × 2048 tokens from WikiText-2 train
- Action space: {2, 4, 8, 16}-bit per head

**Compression**:
- Default: 4× compression (average 4 bits, budget ratio=0.25)
- Constraint: max_2bit ≤ k, where k determined via compounding sweep (k=8 for Qwen 112 heads)
- For Llama/Mistral (256 heads): also use compounding sweep to select k

**Baselines**:
- Uniform 4-bit quantization (all heads at 4-bit)
- Unconstrained greedy allocation (RateQuant-style \cite{zuo2026ratequant})
- Unconstrained MCKP allocation
- L0-random heuristic: Layer-0 heads at 8-bit, k random non-L0 heads at 2-bit, rest at 4-bit (5 seeds, report mean±std and median)
- Naive positional heuristic: Layer-0 at 8-bit, deepest k heads at 2-bit, rest at 4-bit

### §4.2 Main Results (~300 words)
**Table 1** — Cross-architecture main results at 4× compression:

```
\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{PPL ($\downarrow$) on WikiText-2 at 4$\times$ compression. Unconstrained allocation fails catastrophically on \{2,4,8,16\}; our cardinality constraint restores performance. Best constrained result per model in \textbf{bold}.}
\label{tab:main_results}
\begin{tabular}{lcccccc}
\toprule
Model & Baseline & Uniform & \multicolumn{2}{c}{Unconstrained} & Ours \\
 & (bf16) & (4-bit) & Greedy & MCKP & (Constr.) \\
\midrule
Qwen2.5-7B & 9.81 & 15.45 & 32.45 & 36.92 & \textbf{10.91} \\
Llama-3.1-8B & 8.09 & 8.47 & --- & --- & \textbf{8.45} \\
Mistral-7B-v0.3 & 7.04 & 7.13 & --- & --- & 7.16 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}
```

**关键叙述点**:
- Qwen: constrained MCKP achieves 29.3% PPL reduction over uniform (10.91 vs 15.45)
- 没有 constraint 时，greedy (32.45) 和 MCKP (36.92) 都比 uniform (15.45) 差 — catastrophic failure
- Llama: marginal 0.2% improvement (8.45 vs 8.47) — low heterogeneity limits optimization headroom
- Mistral: slightly worse than uniform (7.16 vs 7.13, +0.4%) — genuine negative result; profiler reports near-zero sensitivity differences across heads
- 参考 Figure 3 (\ref{fig:allocation}) 展示 Qwen 的 bit 分配对比
- **注意**：Llama/Mistral 的 unconstrained 结果标 "---" 因为 unconstrained 实验只在 Qwen 上做了

**Figure 3 引用**:
```
\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]{figures/fig3_allocation_comparison.pdf}
\caption{Bit-width allocation comparison on Qwen2.5-7B at 4$\times$ compression. Uniform assigns all heads to 4-bit. Our constrained MCKP protects Layer-0 heads at 8-bit and selectively assigns 8 least-sensitive heads to 2-bit.}
\label{fig:allocation}
\end{figure}
```

### §4.3 Budget Sweep (~200 words)
**Table 3** — Compression ratio ablation on Qwen2.5-7B:

| Compression | Budget | Uniform PPL | Constrained MCKP PPL | Δ PPL |
|------------|--------|-------------|----------------------|-------|
| 2× | 0.50 | 10.10 | 10.66 | −0.56 |
| 4× | 0.25 | 15.45 | 11.23 | +4.21 |
| 8× | 0.125 | 14,759 | 907 | +13,852 |

**叙述**:
- At 2×: uniform 8-bit is near-lossless (+0.29 PPL vs bf16); per-head optimization has no headroom → constrained MCKP slightly worse due to unnecessary 2-bit assignments
- At 4×: sweet spot — 29.3% improvement. Significant gap between uniform 4-bit and optimized allocation.
- At 8×: both methods degrade catastrophically, but constrained MCKP preserves Layer-0 at 8-bit, preventing total collapse (907 vs 14,759). Neither is practical, but demonstrates the protection mechanism.
- 结论: constrained allocation provides meaningful improvement at moderate-to-aggressive compression (≥4×)

### §4.4 Heuristic Baselines (~200 words)

L0-random baseline comparison across 3 models. 用 median 做主对比，supplementary 报 mean±std。

| Model | MCKP | L0-random median | L0-random mean±std | Naive positional |
|-------|------|-----------------|-------------------|-----------------|
| Qwen2.5-7B | 10.91 | 11.52 | 11.69±0.42 | 12.23 |
| Llama-3.1-8B | 8.45 | 10.04 | 10.48±1.03 | — |
| Mistral-7B-v0.3 | 7.32 | 7.59 | 7.56±0.09 | — |

**叙述**:
- Profiling-guided allocation (MCKP) consistently outperforms random L0-based heuristics
- Qwen: MCKP beats L0-random median by 0.61 PPL, naive positional by 1.32 PPL
- Llama: larger gap (MCKP 8.45 vs L0-random median 10.04) — random 2-bit assignment particularly harmful on 256-head architectures
- Mistral: small gap (7.32 vs 7.59) — consistent with low heterogeneity narrative
- High variance of L0-random on Llama (std=1.03) suggests 2-bit assignment is position-sensitive on this architecture

### §4.5 Downstream Evaluation (~200 words)

Qwen2.5-7B, 4× compression, 0-shot evaluation:

| Task | Baseline (bf16) | Uniform 4-bit | MCKP (Ours) | Δ vs Uniform |
|------|-----------------|---------------|-------------|--------------|
| ARC-C | — | 0.482 | 0.514 | +3.2 pts |
| HellaSwag | — | 0.728 | 0.768 | +4.0 pts |
| PIQA | — | 0.766 | 0.779 | +1.3 pts |
| WinoGrande | — | 0.662 | 0.682 | +2.0 pts |
| Average | 0.695 | 0.660 | 0.686 | +2.6 pts |

Recovery rate: (0.686 − 0.660) / (0.695 − 0.660) = 72.8%

**叙述**:
- PPL improvement transfers to downstream tasks: +2.6 points average accuracy over uniform
- Recovery rate 72.8%: constrained MCKP recovers nearly three-quarters of the accuracy lost by uniform 4-bit quantization
- Largest gain on HellaSwag (+4.0 pts) where language modeling quality matters most
- Consistent improvement across all 4 tasks — not cherry-picked

### §3.1 Problem Formulation
- Per-head bit-width allocation as constrained optimization
- Notation（严格使用以下符号）：
  - $h$: KV head index, $h \in \{1,\ldots,H\}$
  - $b_h$: bit-width assigned to head $h$, $b_h \in \mathcal{B}$
  - $\mathcal{B} = \{2, 4, 8, 16\}$: hardware-aligned bit-width set
  - $d_h(b)$: profiled distortion (PPL increase) when head $h$ quantized to $b$ bits
  - $R$: memory budget ratio (e.g. 0.25 for 4× compression)
  - $k$: cardinality constraint — max number of heads at 2-bit
- Objective: minimize $\sum_h d_h(b_h)$ subject to memory budget $\sum_h b_h / (H \cdot 16) \leq R$
- Key distinction from RateQuant: RateQuant operates on consecutive integers {2,3,4,5,6} where polymatroid structure holds (Proposition 6). Hardware requires {2,4,8,16} — non-consecutive, gaps break the structure.

### §3.2 PPL-based Per-Head Profiling
- Quantize each head independently to each $b \in \mathcal{B}$, measure PPL increase $d_h(b)$ over bf16 baseline
- Calibration: 64 sequences × 2048 tokens from WikiText-2 train (hires profiling)
- Additive distortion assumption: total PPL degradation $\approx \sum_h d_h(b_h)$ — valid when distortions are small and independent
- This assumption is what breaks down at 2-bit (§3.3)

### §3.3 Compounding Effect
- WHY additivity fails: when many heads are simultaneously at 2-bit, per-head distortions compound non-additively
- Empirical evidence: unconstrained solvers assign 68–75 heads to 2-bit → actual PPL 32–37, vs predicted ~11 from sum of individual distortions
- Root cause: extreme quantization errors in multiple heads interact through attention computation — each head's output contributes to residual stream, cumulative truncation errors grow super-linearly
- The compounding is specific to 2-bit (not 4-bit or 8-bit) because 2-bit quantization has much larger per-head distortion that saturates the error tolerance
- Reference to Figure 2: U-shaped curve of k vs PPL on Qwen2.5-7B. Data points:
  k=0 (uniform): 15.45
  k=4: 11.77
  k=8: 11.23 (optimal)
  k=10: 11.50
  k=12: 11.42
  k=16: 11.81
  k=24: 13.14
  k=48: 22.88
  k=75: 35.35
  Source: registry experiments compounding_sweep + compounding_sweep_k10_12

### §3.4 Cardinality Constraint
- The fix: add $\sum_h \mathbb{1}[b_h = 2] \leq k$ to the optimization
- k selection: small-scale sweep on calibration data. U-shaped PPL curve → pick the minimum. k=8 for Qwen's 112 heads (~7% of heads)
- Solver-agnostic: the constraint is a single linear inequality, compatible with any solver (greedy, MCKP, ILP)
- Layer-0 protection: the solver automatically avoids 2-bit for Layer-0 heads because their profiled distortion is very high (L0H0: +31.9%, L0H2: +23.2%, L0H3: +11.7%). No manual exclusion needed — the profiler signal is sufficient (exp_d_no_l0_exclusion: 112/112 heads match with and without manual L0 exclusion)

### §3.5 Solver Equivalence
- Key finding: constrained greedy = constrained MCKP (Δ=0.0000 PPL)
- Per-head verification across 3 models:
  - Qwen2.5-7B: 112/112 heads identical allocation
  - Llama-3.1-8B: 256/256 heads identical allocation
  - Mistral-7B-v0.3: 255/256 heads identical (1 head differs: zero-distortion tie, no PPL impact)
- Interpretation: the cardinality constraint narrows the feasible set sufficiently that greedy's locally optimal decisions are globally optimal. The constraint prevents greedy from the cascading 2-bit over-allocation that makes unconstrained greedy suboptimal.
- Practical implication: practitioners can use the simpler O(H log H) greedy algorithm instead of MCKP
- Table 2 (tab2_solver_equivalence): 5 rows showing unconstrained vs constrained for both solvers:
  | Method | Constraint | PPL | Bit Dist {2/4/8/16} | Budget |
  | Greedy unconstrained | None | 32.45 | {68/30/4/10} | 0.25 |
  | MCKP unconstrained | None | 36.92 | {75/33/4/0} | 0.18 |
  | Greedy constrained | max_2bit≤8 | 11.23 | {8/100/4/0} | 0.25 |
  | MCKP constrained | max_2bit≤8 | 11.23 | {8/100/4/0} | 0.25 |
  | Uniform 4-bit | — | 15.45 | {0/112/0/0} | 0.25 |

### §5.1 Heterogeneity Characterization

Per-head 2-bit sensitivity distribution across 3 architectures. 关键概念：

**Top-5% concentration metric**: 将每个 head 的 2-bit distortion $d_h(2)$ 从大到小排序后，top-5% 的 heads 占总 distortion 的比例。高值表示少数 head 极敏感（异质性高），低值表示 head 敏感度均匀。

数据（Director 提供，来自 profiling 数据）：
- **Qwen2.5-7B** (112 heads, GQA 7:1): Top-5% concentration = 0.59–0.66. Layer-0 四个 head 贡献绝大部分 distortion。高异质性 → 非均匀分配大幅受益。
- **Llama-3.1-8B** (256 heads, GQA 4:1): Top-5% concentration = 0.34–0.59. 中等异质性，distortion 分散在更多 heads 上。非均匀分配收益有限。
- **Mistral-7B-v0.3** (256 heads, GQA 4:1, sliding window): Top-5% concentration = 0.42. 多数 head 的 2-bit distortion ≈ 0（profiler 信号近零）。非均匀分配反而有害。

引用 Figure 1 (fig1_head_delta_heatmap): 3-model 并排 heatmap 直观展示 Qwen L0 高 delta vs Mistral 全面低 delta。

Qwen2.5-7B (left) shows high concentration in Layer-0 heads; Llama-3.1-8B (center) shows moderate spread; Mistral-7B-v0.3 (right) shows near-zero sensitivity across all heads. Color intensity indicates PPL increase when the head is quantized to 2-bit.}

### §5.2 Diagnostic Framework

Practitioner decision framework:
1. **Run per-head profiling** (same as §3.2)
2. **Compute Top-5% concentration**:
   - > 0.50 → non-uniform allocation recommended (Qwen case: 29.3% PPL improvement)
   - 0.30–0.50 → marginal, depends on compression ratio (Llama case: 0.2% at 4×)
   - Total profiling distortion ≈ 0 for most heads → use uniform directly (Mistral case: profiler has no reliable signal, non-uniform is counterproductive)
3. Key insight: the diagnostic is cheap (profiling is already needed for allocation) and avoids wasted computation on architectures that won't benefit

### §5.3 Aggressive Compression Amplifies Benefit

Even low-heterogeneity models benefit from non-uniform allocation at more aggressive compression ratios:

**5.3× compression** (budget = 0.1875, average 3 bits):
- Llama: constrained MCKP = 57.60 vs uniform 2-bit = 2643.77 (45× better)
- Mistral: constrained MCKP = 11.91 vs uniform 2-bit = 519.11 (44× better)
Source: registry llama_aggressive_compression, mistral_aggressive_compression

**8× compression** (budget = 0.125):
- Llama: MCKP = 2372.33 vs uniform = 2643.77 (barely better, both catastrophic)
- Mistral: MCKP = 399.90 vs uniform = 519.11 (1.3× better)

Key message: at 4× compression, Mistral 的 non-uniform 反而有害 (+0.4%)。但在 5.3×，MCKP 比 uniform 好 44×。原因：5.3× 压缩下必须使用大量 2-bit heads，此时 constrained allocation 保护关键 heads 的作用被放大。

跨架构一致性：Llama 45× vs Mistral 44×，倍率高度一致，说明 constrained allocation 的保护机制是架构无关的。

### §5.4 Profiling Resolution

Hires (64 seq × 2048 tok) vs standard (16 seq × 512 tok) profiling on Qwen2.5-7B:

- Standard profiling MCKP PPL: 11.23
- Hires profiling MCKP PPL: 10.91
- Improvement: 0.32 PPL absolute
- Degradation above baseline: standard = 1.42 (11.23 - 9.81), hires = 1.10 (10.91 - 9.81), reduction = 22.5%
- Non-zero 2-bit delta signals: standard = 37/112 heads, hires = 100/112 heads (2.7× more)
- Allocation changes: 8/112 heads differ — hires protects shallow layers (L1-L3) and is more aggressive in mid-layers (L5-L11)

Source: registry exp_e_hires_profile (profile_resolution data)

### §5.5 KV Separation Ablation

KV heads 分离优化（K 和 V 作为独立 items 分别分配 bit-width）：

- Joint K=V MCKP: 10.91 PPL (K 和 V 共享 bit-width)
- Separated K/V MCKP: 11.22 PPL (+0.303 worse)
- Root cause: K-side max_2bit doubled to 16 (vs joint's 8), causing K over-compression. V distortion near-zero → all V at 4-bit.
- 21/112 heads show K≠V asymmetry, all with K < V (K gets more aggressively compressed)
- Conclusion: joint allocation sufficient under current constraints; K/V separated allocation with per-side cardinality constraints is future work.

Source: registry kv_separation

\section{Analysis}
\label{sec:analysis}

\subsection{Heterogeneity Characterization}
\label{sec:heterogeneity}

The benefit of non-uniform allocation depends on how unevenly head sensitivities are distributed.
We quantify this with a \emph{top-5\% concentration metric}: sort per-head 2-bit distortions $d_h(2)$ in descending order and compute the fraction of total distortion contributed by the top 5\% of heads.
High concentration indicates that a few heads are disproportionately sensitive; low concentration indicates near-uniform sensitivity.

Table~\ref{tab:heterogeneity} summarizes the results across three architectures at $4\times$ compression.
Qwen2.5-7B exhibits the highest heterogeneity (top-5\% concentration 0.59--0.66), with Layer-0 heads contributing the majority of total 2-bit distortion.
Constrained MCKP reduces degradation from $+$5.64 PPL (uniform) to $+$1.42 PPL, a 27.3\% improvement over uniform 4-bit.
Llama-3.1-8B shows moderate heterogeneity (0.34--0.59), and the allocation benefit is marginal ($+$0.36 vs.\ $+$0.38).
Mistral-7B-v0.3 has a concentration of 0.42 but near-zero absolute distortion for most heads, leaving the profiler with no reliable signal.
Here, constrained MCKP is slightly \emph{worse} than uniform ($+$0.13 vs.\ $+$0.10), confirming that non-uniform allocation is counterproductive when heterogeneity is low.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\small
\caption{Head sensitivity heterogeneity and constrained allocation benefit across architectures at 4$\times$ compression.}
\label{tab:heterogeneity}
\begin{tabular}{lccccc}
\toprule
Model & GQA & Top-5\% & $\Delta$ PPL & $\Delta$ PPL & Recommendation \\
 & Ratio & Conc. & (Uniform) & (Ours) & \\
\midrule
Qwen2.5-7B & 7:1 & 0.59--0.66 & $+$5.64 & $+$1.42 & Non-uniform \\
Llama-3.1-8B & 4:1 & 0.34--0.59 & $+$0.38 & $+$0.36 & Marginal \\
Mistral-7B-v0.3 & 4:1 & 0.42 & $+$0.10 & $+$0.13 & Uniform \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\begin{figure*}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\textwidth]{figures/fig1_head_delta_heatmap.pdf}
\caption{Per-head 2-bit quantization sensitivity across three models. Qwen2.5-7B (left) shows high concentration in Layer-0 heads; Llama-3.1-8B (center) shows moderate spread; Mistral-7B-v0.3 (right) shows near-zero sensitivity across all heads. Color intensity indicates PPL increase when the head is quantized to 2-bit.}
\label{fig:heatmap}
\end{figure*}

Figure~\ref{fig:heatmap} visualizes the per-head 2-bit distortion as a heatmap.
The contrast is stark: Qwen's Layer-0 heads show high distortion (dark cells) while mid-to-deep layers are near-zero; Mistral shows uniformly low distortion across all layers and heads.

\subsection{Diagnostic Framework}
\label{sec:diagnostic}

The heterogeneity characterization yields a practical decision procedure for practitioners:

\begin{enumerate}[nosep]
\item Run per-head profiling as described in \S\ref{sec:profiling}.
\item Compute the top-5\% concentration from the resulting distortion table.
\item Select allocation strategy:
  \begin{itemize}[nosep]
  \item Concentration ${>}\,0.50$: non-uniform allocation recommended (Qwen case; 27.3\% PPL improvement).
  \item Concentration $0.30$--$0.50$: marginal benefit; depends on target compression ratio (Llama case; 0.2\% at $4\times$).
  \item Near-zero absolute distortion for most heads: use uniform directly (Mistral case; non-uniform is counterproductive).
  \end{itemize}
\end{enumerate}

The diagnostic adds no computational overhead: it reuses the profiling data already required for the allocation solver.
This avoids wasted optimization effort on architectures where non-uniform allocation provides no benefit.

\subsection{Aggressive Compression Amplifies Benefit}
\label{sec:aggressive}

At $4\times$ compression, Llama and Mistral show minimal benefit from non-uniform allocation.
At more aggressive compression ratios, the picture changes.

At $5.3\times$ compression (budget ratio 0.1875, average 3 bits), constrained MCKP provides large improvements on both architectures.
On Llama, constrained MCKP achieves 57.60 PPL vs.\ uniform 2-bit at 2643.77---a $45\times$ reduction.
On Mistral, the gap is comparable: 11.91 vs.\ 519.11 ($44\times$).
The consistency of this ratio across architectures ($45\times$ vs.\ $44\times$) indicates that the constrained allocation's protection mechanism is architecture-independent.

At $8\times$ compression (budget ratio 0.125), the benefit narrows.
Llama: 2372.33 vs.\ 2643.77 (both catastrophic).
Mistral: 399.90 vs.\ 519.11 ($1.3\times$ better, but neither is usable).

The mechanism is clear: $5.3\times$ compression forces extensive use of 2-bit heads, and constrained allocation protects the sensitive heads from 2-bit assignment.
At $4\times$, the budget is generous enough that uniform 4-bit already works well for low-heterogeneity models.
At $8\times$, the budget is too constrained for any allocation to preserve quality.
The intermediate regime ($5.3\times$) is where constrained allocation provides the largest relative benefit.

\subsection{Profiling Resolution}
\label{sec:profiling_resolution}

We compare standard-resolution profiling (16 sequences $\times$ 512 tokens) against high-resolution profiling (64 sequences $\times$ 2048 tokens) on Qwen2.5-7B at $4\times$ compression.

High-resolution profiling improves constrained MCKP from 11.23 to 10.91 PPL ($-$0.32 absolute).
Relative to the bf16 baseline (9.81), this reduces the degradation from 1.42 to 1.10, a 22.5\% reduction.
The improvement comes from finer-grained sensitivity estimates: standard profiling detects non-zero 2-bit distortion in 37 of 112 heads, while high-resolution profiling detects 100 of 112 (2.7$\times$ more).

The additional signal changes 8 of 112 head assignments.
High-resolution profiling protects shallow layers (L1--L3) at higher bit-widths while compressing mid-layers (L5--L11) more aggressively---a redistribution that standard profiling misses because its distortion estimates for these heads fall below the noise floor.

\subsection{KV Separation Ablation}
\label{sec:kv_separation}

We test whether treating K and V caches as independent items in the MCKP solver---allowing different bit-widths for K and V within the same head---improves over joint allocation where K and V share a bit-width.

Joint allocation achieves 10.91 PPL; separated K/V allocation achieves 11.22 ($+$0.31 worse).
The degradation stems from K-side over-compression: the separated solver doubles the maximum number of 2-bit K items to 16 (vs.\ 8 in the joint formulation), since K and V are counted independently against the cardinality constraint.
Meanwhile, V-side distortion is near-zero for most heads, so the solver assigns all V items to 4-bit, concentrating compression entirely on K.

Of the 112 heads, 21 show K$\neq$V asymmetry in the separated allocation, all with K receiving a lower bit-width than V.
This systematic asymmetry suggests that K caches are inherently more compressible than V caches, consistent with the observation that key vectors primarily encode positional information while value vectors carry content.

Joint allocation is sufficient under the current constraint formulation.
Separated K/V allocation with per-side cardinality constraints---limiting 2-bit assignments independently for K and V---is a direction for future work.
